response.rationale: R3 is the most complete: it integrates the classic dermatomyositis phenotype (Gottron papules, nailfold capillary changes, proximal weakness, elevated CK/aldolase, MRI STIR hyperintensity) with the causal ipilimumab timeline and recurrence on rechallenge. R1 has the phenotype but omits the drug causation; R5, R4, and R2 each explain only a fragment and are contradicted by the remaining findings. The post-steroid biopsy without inflammation is a limitation but does not override the clinical picture.

rejected.why: Temporal skin eruption only; does not explain Gottron papules, nailfold capillary changes, proximal weakness, elevated CK/aldolase, or MRI muscle hyperintensity.
Explains muscle weakness and CK but cannot account for heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, or nailfold capillary changes; biopsy lacks inflammatory myositis.
ANA and photodistributed erythema are nonspecific; fails to explain Gottron papules, nailfold capillary changes, proximal weakness, elevated CK, and MRI muscle hyperintensity.
